title: Tagged blocks that leave the context — and the four ways they only look like they did
why: `ctxdiff tokens` names a block the developer TAGGED that entered an agent's context and later left it for good — 'the block you tagged rag at turn 1 was evicted at turn 4'. That sentence is only worth printing if it is never printed wrongly, so this fixture is mostly counter-examples. Session 1 (one agent) carries: a tagged block that really is evicted and never returns (reported); a second tagged block that is absent for one turn and BACK the next (not reported — it was crowded out, not forgotten); a tagged block whose text is EDITED in place, which the differ classifies as 'modified' and a naive hash-presence scan would call an eviction; and ordinary heuristically-labeled history that is evicted every turn and must stay silent, since that is what a context window IS. Session 2 interleaves two agents so the writer's turn cannot make the researcher's tagged block look lost — a hand-off is not an eviction — and then evicts it for real on the researcher's own timeline, which is the case that must carry an [agent:researcher] chip. The block token counts are also the fixture for `--context-window`: turn totals here are small and stable, so a percentage regression shows up as a one-character diff.
why_session_3: Sessions 1 and 2 both set `tags` on EVERY call, and that is not what capture produces — it is what HID a bug that made this whole feature silent. `tracer.tag()` buffers labels for the NEXT recorded call and clears itself, so a block tagged once is stored `label_source='tagged'` on exactly ONE call and `heuristic` on every later call that still carries the same text. Session 3 is therefore the REAL-WORLD shape and the README's own advertised sentence: `tags` on the first call only, the retrieved policy present on turns 1-4, and a summarizer rebuilding a shorter history at turn 5 that drops it for good. A detector that decides taggedness from the older side of the evicting pair reports NOTHING here — `evictions: []`, no stanza in `tokens`, and `check --no-tagged-eviction` printing 'all 1 tagged block survived 4 turn pairs' and exiting 0. The ordinary history the same rebuild threw away (two questions and two answers, heuristically labeled) must stay silent in the same output, which is what makes this a test of the narrowing and not just of the fix.
